chunks: Beware! I have called you to fight these people night and day, secretly and openly,
and I said to you: Attack them before they attack you, for by Allah, no people have ever been attacked in the heart of their homes but they suffered disgrace;
but you procrastinated and forsook one another until raids were launched against you and your homelands were conquered.
And this is the brother of Ghamid; his cavalry has reached al-Anbar and killed Hassan ibn Hassan al-Bakri, and has removed your cavalry from their garrisons.

key_terms.أَخُو غَامِدٍ: the brother of Ghamid (referring to a specific leader or tribe member)
key_terms.عُقْرِ دَارِهِمْ: in the heart of their homes

ai.seo_question: What criticism did Imam Ali make regarding the Muslims' approach to jihad in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from the Sermon of Exhortation (Khutbat al-Jihad) highlights the strategic principle of preemptive warfare, where Imam Ali (AS) argues that allowing enemies to strike first within one's own territory leads to inevitable humiliation and loss of sovereignty. The specific reference to Banu Ghamid's raid on al-Anbar and the death of Hassan ibn al-Bakri serves as a concrete historical example of the consequences of the people's procrastination (tawaakul) and neglect (takhaazul). This sermon underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on active defense and political vigilance as religious duties, linking military readiness directly to the preservation of the community's dignity and lands.
